name: James Craggs the younger

summary.text: James Craggs the younger was Secretary of State at the time of the South Sea Bubble. According to Britannica, the South Sea directors gave him at least £30,000 in company stock; he broke down under examination by a parliamentary committee and died in 1721 on the eve of his trial, a death widely believed at the time to be suicide.

facts.claim: Britannica states that the South Sea directors gave Craggs at least £30,000 in company stock.
facts.quote: the directors gave him at least £30,000 in company stock

facts.claim: Craggs broke down under examination by a parliamentary committee, and his death on the eve of his trial was generally believed to be a confession of guilt by suicide.
facts.quote: he broke down under examination by a parliamentary committee, and his mysterious death on the eve of his trial was generally believed to be a confession of guilt by suicide

connections.claim: Britannica states the South Sea Company's directors gave Craggs at least £30,000 in stock.
connections.quote: the directors gave him at least £30,000 in company stock

openQuestions: Site claim tested: the page's £574,500 'fictitious stock' figure was not found in the sources returned; Britannica gives £30,000 for Craggs alone.
The 1721 estates report concerned Craggs senior (the Postmaster General), not the Secretary of State; the page does not distinguish the two.
A 1721 report on the estates of the directors, Aislabie and Craggs senior (presented 6 February 1721) appears in library catalogues; it was not opened and is not cited.
